item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
612
ABPZ20 KNHC 201741
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located located over a thousand miles southwest of the
southern tip of Baja California.

Southwest of Southwestern Mexico (EP99):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located about 350 miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico have
changed little in organization since earlier today. However,
environmental conditions remain conducive for development, and an
increase in the organization of the system could result in it
becoming a tropical depression or storm within the next day or so.
The system is expected to move eastward off the coast of southern
Mexico on Monday, but could begin moving toward the coast by late
Tuesday. Interests along the southwestern and west-central coast of
Mexico should monitor the progress of this system. For more
information, including gale warnings, see the High Seas Forecast
issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands, remain limited. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some development of this system by the middle to latter portion
of this week as the system moves westward to west-southwestward, and
a tropical depression could form to the south or southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands once the environment becomes more favorable.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Odalys are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast Advisories on Tropical Storm Odalys are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Katz/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 202047
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Odalys Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
...ODALYS EXPECTED TO BECOME A HURRICANE IN A DAY OR SO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.7N 126.6W
ABOUT 1345 MI...2160 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was
located near latitude 11.7 North, longitude 126.6 West. Odalys is
moving toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and a turn
to the northwest is expected later today followed by a turn to the 
east on Tuesday.  A gradual turn toward the east-northeast is 
expected by the middle part of the week followed by a turn toward 
the northeast by the end of the week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Continued gradual strengthening is expected
during the next 48 hours, and Odalys is forecast to become a
hurricane by Monday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 202048
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
Odalys continues to gradually become better organized, with very 
deep convection near and over the center, and some banding features 
evident over the southern semicircle.  Upper-level outflow remains 
somewhat restricted over the northern quadrant of the circulation, 
however.  This implies some northerly vertical wind shear over the 
storm.  The estimated current intensity is increased to 45 kt based 
on objective and subjective Dvorak estimates and observations from 
a scatterometer overpass.

The tropical cyclone is expected to be in an environment of 
low to moderate shear, over very warm waters, and within a moist 
low- to mid-level air mass for the next couple of days.  Therefore 
continued strengthening is forecast for the next couple of days.  
Later in the forecast period, somewhat drier air and the possible 
inhibiting influence of a developing tropical cyclone to the east 
could limit strengthening.  The official intensity forecast is 
close to the model consensus.

Odalys should move generally northwestward through tonight, on the 
southwest side of a mid-level ridge.  In 24-48 hours, a 500 mb 
trough moving into California and Baja California should cause the 
system to turn eastward.  Later in the forecast period, as the 
trough lifts out, Odalys is likely to move northeastward on the 
northwestern side of a mid-level ridge.  The developing tropical 
cyclone to the east could also have some influence on the track in 
3-5 days, although there is considerable uncertainty about this.
